chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Hakim, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from al-Husayn ibn Hammad, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When I prostrate, my forehead falls on the raised spot.' He said, 'Raise your head, then place it [down again].'
ai.seo_question: What should one do if their forehead touches a raised bump while prostrating in prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the technical requirement of *istiqamat* (stability) in the forehead's placement during *sujdah*, ensuring the contact is firm and not obstructed by uneven surfaces. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the precision of physical acts of worship, where the validity of prostration depends on the forehead resting directly on the pure, flat surface of the prayer mat (*sajjada*). This ruling underscores the principle that minor physical impediments to the prescribed posture must be corrected to maintain the ritual's integrity.
